result.title: Your Agent Acts Differently When You're Around: How User Presence Changes Agent Behavior in Negotiation
result.summary: LLM agents increasingly interact with other agents on behalf of users, yet how users in the loop affect their agents' behavior--for better or worse--remains poorly understood. We study this question through the lens of negotiation, where agents must represent users while strategically bargaining with other agents. To isolate the effect of user presence, we develop PRESENT, a controlled evaluation framework that compares negotiation settings with and without an interactive user, while holding the game, objectives, and user preferences fixed across conditions. Across 11.2k runs spanning 7 games and 8 models, we find that user presence significantly changes both outcomes and behavior. Specifically, negotiation parties with a user obtain higher payouts (+13.7% on average) and their agents negotiate more aggressively. Surprisingly, user presence also induces misaligned behavior, both toward counterparties (where its rate roughly doubles) and toward users (where it emerges in 14.3% of games). These misaligned behaviors are uncorrelated with outcomes and persist even when the user sends only templated, neutral messages. These findings expose two blind spots in current evaluation practice: static instructions miss behaviors that emerge only when users are present, and outcome-level metrics cannot detect them.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 PRESENT 控制实验框架，在固定博弈与用户偏好的条件下比较有无交互用户参与时 LLM 谈判智能体的行为与收益差异，并报告用户在场带来的更激进谈判、更高收益以及向对手和用户两侧出现的错位行为。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作聚焦多智能体谈判中的用户在场效应与对齐评测，不涉及视觉信息保留、latent 推理状态生成或证据筛选，也无可核查的状态更新、监督或停止决策线索，故排除。
